licences.notes: Words as printed in the Peters vocal score: o ti so pentir (the libretto has fo), Don Alfonso's se costei non ci ravvisa (the libretto has li), Mi da without its accent, c'e in two of the three non c'è più, quì, di grazia pieni (the libretto has grazie), and dell' enorme, dell' uso and quell' aspetto as two words.

licences.source: Edition Peters vocal score (Edition Peters Nr. 4474, plate 11446, edited by Georg Schünemann), pages 91–109, bars 1–220 of No. 13
licences.author: Kurt Soldan (1891–1946), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: sung lines and piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge (in five page ranges), a separate sweep for dynamics and other marks, then checked bar by bar by five fresh checkers (all clean). The German singing translation is left out. All six singers have a staff throughout, with rests where the print leaves a staff out. Bar 1 is a one-quarter upbeat, set as 1/4; bar 127 is a bar's rest with a fermata. Where a beamed pair of eighths carries two crowded syllables, they are sung on the first note (na_ho, ma_in, to_e), except in bars 193 and 199, where the print spaces them on separate notes. Kept as printed: the left hand's dotted half F with a second F stem on beat 3 in bar 91. Print slips set right: in bar 113 the right hand's first two chords are both printed as quarters and are written eighth + quarter; in bar 109 only one flat is printed in the right hand, and the upper note is written E flat, as Fiordiligi sings it; bar 220's right hand is filled out with a hidden quarter rest. Playback tempo ♩ = 132, ♩ = 165 from the Allegro in 3/4 (bar 55) and a half note = 110 (♩ = 220) from the Molto Allegro (bar 128), about 4 minutes 40 seconds, a little slower than Jacobs (4:23); Mozart gives the words only.
